summary.intent: Execute phase 20 (vault-migration) of the cipher-box project using GSD wave-based parallel execution, then perform a security review and code cleanup of all phase 20 work.
summary.outcome: All 4 plans executed successfully across 3 waves. Two HIGH security issues were fixed (key length bounds checking, sensitive field redaction in Debug impls). Code simplification fixed a duplicate HKDF derivation and a double ECIES wrap in desktop vault init. Phase 20 checkpoint is still pending human verification of the web client login flow.

repo: The project uses GSD (get-shit-done) workflow system with wave-based parallel plan execution via subagents.
cipher-box uses a vault blob v2 binary format for IPFS-stored encrypted vault keys, replacing the previous DB-stored approach.
The migration is lazy: non-migrated users trigger migration on first login; migrated users read rootFolderKey from IPFS v2 blob via HKDF-derived IPNS keypair.

orval (API client codegen) generates `{ [key: string]: unknown } | null` instead of `string | null` for nullable string fields — this is a known orval bug requiring `as unknown as string` casts as the correct workaround.
The project has a custom security:review skill that produces structured reports to `.planning/security/REVIEW-[timestamp].md`.
Desktop (Tauri/Rust) and web client both need to handle v2 blob format; Rust implementation lives in `src/crypto/vault_blob.rs`.

code.finding: serialize_vault_blob_v2 was changed to return Result to enforce key length bounds checking — all callers needed updating to handle the Result.
InitVaultRequest and VaultResponse were using derived Debug which would log encrypted key material. Fixed with custom Debug impls that redact sensitive fields.
Had a double ECIES wrap — the already-wrapped key was being re-wrapped before vault init. Fixed to reuse the existing wrapped key.
PATH A (migrated user login) had duplicate HKDF derivation. Simplified to derive once and reuse.

orval generates object type instead of string for nullable fields — adding `type: String` to the NestJS DTO does not fix this because the OpenAPI spec was already correct. The bug is in orval's handling of nullable string schemas.

workflow: GSD init tool must be run from the correct working directory — phase dirs may be siblings of the main repo (e.g. cipher-box-phase-20), not inside it.
Security review skill can be run inline during a GSD checkpoint pause to review implementation before approving continuation.
When orval codegen doesn't fix a type issue after DTO changes, check if the OpenAPI spec actually changed before pursuing further — the spec may already be correct and the bug is in orval itself.
The classifyHandoffIfNeeded error is a Claude Code runtime bug (fires post-completion), not a GSD failure — spot-check SUMMARY.md + git commits to determine actual success.

friction: GSD init tool failed on first run because it was executed from the wrong directory (cipher-box instead of cipher-box-phase-20).
API error (ConnectionRefused) interrupted the first security review invocation, requiring a retry.

orval codegen investigation consumed multiple tool calls before confirming the `as unknown as string` casts are the correct/unavoidable workaround for a pre-existing orval bug — DTO change had to be reverted.
serialize_vault_blob_v2 return type change to Result required updating multiple call sites (vault.rs, fuse/mod.rs) and all test calls in vault_blob.rs.
open_items: Human verification of plan 20-04 still pending: login with non-migrated account to trigger lazy migration, re-login to verify IPFS v2 blob PATH A, test /recovery.html both methods.
M-1: Recovery tool private key not zeroed after use.
M-2: No dedup guard on concurrent migration from multiple browser tabs — could cause duplicate migration calls.
M-3: Unnecessary ECIES re-wrap on every root folder publish (redundant crypto work on each write).
L-1: Zero-length key accepted by deserializers (bounds check only enforces upper bound).
L-2: No SRI hashes on CDN scripts in recovery.html.
orval nullable string type generation bug tracked as known issue — `as unknown as string` casts remain in codebase as workaround.
